title: Hub GCSE History Topic Checklist (Aligned to Edexcel 1HI0)
subtitle: Option 13: Migrants in Britain, c800–present and Notting Hill, c1948–c1970

exam_structure.paper_name: Paper 1: Thematic Study and Historic Environment
exam_structure.overview: Section A tests the Historic Environment site (16 marks, 25 mins). Section B tests the Thematic Study across 4 eras (36 marks, 55 mins) plus 4 marks for SPaG.

topics.title: 1. The context for migration
points: Causes of migration & patterns of settlement (incl. Vikings, Normans, Jews & other European traders & craftsmen)
Context of English society: landownership & the growth of towns; wool industry; opportunities for migrants; the role the monarchy (incl. the need for royal finance); England as a part of Christendom

topics.title: 2. The experience and impact of migrants
points: Experience of migrants in England: their relations with the authorities & the existing population (incl. the legal status of ‘alien’ & the impact of the Black Death)
Impact of migrants in England (incl. the Danelaw, culture, trade & the built environment)

topics.title: 3. Case study
points: City of York under the Vikings

topics.title: 2. The experience and impact of migrants
points: Experience of migrants in England: their relations with the authorities & the existing population
Impact of migrants in England (incl. culture, trade, industry & agriculture)

topics.title: 3. Case studies
points: Sandwich & Canterbury in the sixteenth century: the experiences of Flemish & Walloon migrants & their role in the local economy
Experience of Huguenots in seventeenth century England

sections.title: c1700–c1900: Migration in eighteenth- and nineteenth-century Britain

topics.title: 1. The context for migration
points: Change & continuity in reasons for migration & patterns of settlement (incl. migrants from Ireland, Europe & the Empire)
Changing context of British society: changing social structures; the Industrial Revolution; urbanisation; transatlantic slavery; the growth of the British Empire; civil liberties

topics.title: 2. The experience and impact of migrants
points: Experience of migrants in Britain: their relations with the authorities & the existing population; media
Impact of migrants in Britain (incl. culture, trade & industry, politics & the urban environment)

topics.title: 3. Case studies
points: Liverpool in the nineteenth century: its role in migration & the experiences of migrants (incl. Irish migrants)
Experience of Jewish migrants in the East End of London in late nineteenth c entury

topics.title: 1. The context for migration
points: Change & continuity in reasons for migration & patterns of settlement (incl. migrants from Ireland, Europe, the British Empire & the Commonwealth); refugees & asylum seekers

Changing context of British society: the World Wars; the end of the British Empire, decolonisation & the development of the Commonwealth; EU membership; legislation on immigration & nationality (incl. the Aliens Act (1905) & British Nationality Acts)

topics.title: 2. The experience and impact of migrants
points: Experience of migrants in Britain: their relations with the authorities & the existing population (incl. anti-immigration & equal rights movements); The Race Relations Act (1965); media
Impact of migrants in Britain (incl. culture, politics, the urban environment, public services & the economy)

topics.title: 3. Case studies
points: Bristol in the mid-twentieth century: the experiences of migrants & their impact on society
Experience of Asian migrants in Leicester from 1945; Notting Hill, c1948–c1970 The historic environment

topics.title: 1. Notting Hill, c1948–c1970
points: Local context of Notting Hill; reasons for Caribbean migration to the area; problems of housing: houses of multiple occupation (HMOs), overcrowding & slum landlords, e.g. Peter Rachman; Bruce Kenrick & the Notting Hill Housing Trust; development of Portobello Road market

Influence of Caribbean cultures on the area, in particular the development of shops, markets, cafes & restaurants, shebeens, nightclubs & entertainment which featured Caribbean food & music; development of All Saints Road; Mutual self-help organisations, e.g. ‘pardner’ schemes

Racism & policing; The Notting Hill Riots (1958); murder of Kelso Cochrane & the reaction of the local community; impact of anti-immigrant groups (incl. Oswald Mosley’s Union Movement & his 1959 election campaign)

Black activism in the Notting Hill area; Claudia Jones & the West Indian Gazette; The 1959 Caribbean Carnival & the later development of the Notting Hill Carnival; Frank Crichlow & the Mangrove Restaurant; The British Black Panthers; The ‘Mangrove Nine’

National & regional context: Britain after the Second World War, reconstruction & demand for labour; the connection to the British Empire & Commonwealth; The ‘Swinging Sixties’; Poverty in London; Policing in London

topics.title: 2. Knowledge, selection and use of sources for historical enquiries
points: Local source types: local newspapers, publications written for the Caribbean community, local council & police records, housing & employment records, oral & written memoirs of local residents, photographs
National source types: national newspapers, photographs, government records, census data, opinion polls, television reports, memoirs
Evaluating source strengths & limitations for historical enquiries
Formulating targeted follow-up questions for historical enquiries
Selecting relevant archival sources for follow-up investigations
